terra.problem: The junk-drawer joke switches from resting in God to taking a nap, and resting on one's own strength does not explain why the nap was short. The comparison fails the joke logic test.
David states his confidence that he will never be shaken. Calling it a promise adds something the verse does not say.
Their intention does not establish that David knows exactly what will happen.
The third-time punchline plays on the psalm's once-and-twice wording. The way Scripture is written must not be the joke.
David being a king is a Bible fact not stated in Psalm 62, so it needs a reference.
The explanation claims that repayment according to deeds makes the earlier scale picture make sense. The psalm does not state that connection.
The explanation turns birth into where a person was born. The earlier contrast is between lowborn and exalted people, not places of birth.
